expectations.evidence: Document only mentions VS-NfD as 'the lowest classification tier' but does not enumerate all four German classification levels (VS-NfD, VS-Vertraulich, Geheim, Streng Geheim).

Extensive detail: references BSI-Standards 200-1/200-2/200-3, Schutzbedarf levels, Sicherheitskonzept requirement, UP Bund, SiSyPHuS hardening, ISO 27001 auf Basis von IT-Grundschutz certification, and verinice tooling.
Section 5 covers C5:2020 in depth: 125 criteria across 17 domains listed, Type 2 attestation explained, ISAE 3402 audit process, phased roadmap with timelines, and annual re-attestation.

Section 2.2 and Section 6.4 detail VS-NfD-freigegebene products: SINA Box, genuscreen, NCP VS GovNet Connector for VPN; secunet sure for disk encryption; SINA Workstations. Procurement table in Section 9.1 with lead times.

BSI TR-02102 (Parts 1-4) explicitly referenced in Sections 2.1, 3.6, and 5.2. Specific algorithms listed: AES-256, RSA >= 3000 bit, brainpoolP256r1 curves (BSI-preferred over NIST), TLS 1.2/1.3 with approved cipher suites, SHA-256.

Executive summary states 'All data processing and storage occurs exclusively within the Federal Republic of Germany.' Section 6.3: 'VS-NfD data must never leave German territory.' No federation to foreign sites. Backup must remain in physically secured areas within Germany.

Section 4.1 lists 18 specific Bausteine by ID and German title (OPS.1.1.3, SYS.1.5, NET.1.1, INF.2, CON.1, DER.1, etc.) with application notes for each. Schutzbedarf analysis and Risikoanalyse methodology also described.

Section 2.2 provides structured analysis of where FLOSS is permissible, where BSI-approved products are mandatory, and grey areas. Section 7 gives a full decision matrix across 13 layers with viability assessment. Concludes ~80% FLOSS feasible.

Section 3.7 maps OpenStack services to architecture roles. Section 4.1 maps Grundschutz Bausteine to OpenStack components (SYS.1.5 for KVM/Nova, NET.1.1 for OVN/Neutron, etc.). Section 3.3 cites SYS.1.5 for hypervisor. Architecture diagrams show how OpenStack fits the zone model.
GDPR (DSGVO) is mentioned briefly in the regulations table. However, NIS2 and EUCS (EU Cloud Certification Scheme) are entirely absent from the document.

Section 5.3 provides a detailed 5-phase attestation roadmap spanning ~20 months. Section 5.4 covers IT-Grundschutz certification with 3-year validity and annual surveillance audits. Continuous compliance phase described.

Architecture is entirely German/EU-oriented: BSI standards, German products (SINA, genuscreen, secunet), German agencies (CERT-Bund, ITZBund, BWI), brainpool curves preferred over NIST, EU-manufactured hardware recommended, German procurement entities (govdigital, Dataport). No FedRAMP, NIST SP 800, or US-centric references.
